note: Blind read (Opus, fenced from cruces). 8 sites, all OURS, all repaired. ⭐⭐⭐ MARQUEE: 0605D the lemma *Occurram* rendered 'I may attain' — Douay's word for Phil 3:11 — while the gloss that exists to expound the verb literally (*occurram Christo*, *occurrent Domino in aera*) had it rendered 'meet' twice within four lines. The lexical hinge was severed and two Latin verbs collapsed onto one English word. Now three verbs, three Englishes. ⭐⭐⭐ 0607A: the lemma supplied *meum*/*mea* — EXACTLY the possessives its OWN [var:] declared to be the Vulgate's and not Migne's. A NEW SHAPE: the conformation hid inside the entry that was catching the conformation. ⭐⭐ 0601D: A COLUMN ANCHOR PRESENT, VERBATIM, IN ORDER, AND ~55 WORDS DOWNSTREAM OF ITS WORD. Measured, not conjectured: the words that moved between bands carry no colon, semicolon or question mark, so the band test returned 0 mismatches BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER the repair. Invisible to both mechanical checks; verify-english checks anchor presence and order, never position. Also 0608B a connective duplicated INTO the lemma italics (span count right, contents wrong); 0606C an *et...et* flattened; 0605D a supplied 'his' importing the Vulgate's *morti eius*; 0604A *ejus* losing its printed not-the-subject signal. CARMEN CHRISTI ZERO UPHELD by independent collation of all twelve lemmata — Migne genuinely agrees with the Clementine there, so there was nothing to conform; the 0604B De dono perseverantiae excerpt clean on all five negatives. ⚑ The read proved something about the translator's own hand-off: it named five hardest passages, ALL of which held, while both substantive defects sat where it had written 'settled' — one lemma recorded as AGREEING with the Vulgate, one the subject of a starred crux.
